analysis: The option addresses sustainable production through life-cycle assessment, energy conversion and design, resource recovery experiments, environmental chemistry and product design. Biochemistry and the life-science laboratory supply molecular and experimental foundations. Linear algebra, numerical methods and feedback support mathematical study of resource and dynamic systems. Resource recovery, life-cycle accounting and technical-economic energy design are sustained programme components. They do not supply the integrated chemistry, thermodynamics, transport and plant engineering of the external degree.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Academic writing, evidence literacy, presentation and reflective development support the common foundation; this is common academic formation and distinct from the required engineering research project.

BENENTR111.name: Consumer Product Design
BENENTR111.contribution: develops a product concept, fabrication method and prototype and evaluates sustainability and cost; it supports chemical-product design questions without teaching chemical synthesis or process equipment

DISGATE101.name: Introduction to Programming
DISGATE101.contribution: supplies structured programming, testing and debugging for quantitative analysis and system models

DISGATE102.name: Mathematical Methods
DISGATE102.contribution: introduces single-variable calculus, complex numbers and differential equations for scientific modelling

DISMATH211.name: Linear Algebra
DISMATH211.contribution: uses matrix systems, eigenvalues and least-squares methods for quantitative models

DISMATH213.name: Computational & Numerical Methods
DISMATH213.contribution: teaches stable numerical solution methods for equations, interpolation, integration and differential equations

DISMATH312.name: Linear Systems
DISMATH312.contribution: uses differential equations, Laplace transforms, frequency response and feedback to model dynamic systems

DISMATH314.name: Probability & Statistics
DISMATH314.contribution: develops probability, distributions, estimation and simulation for experimental and model uncertainty

ENSDELT311.name: R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation
ENSDELT311.contribution: uses laboratory work on metal recovery, solar-panel recycling and remediation to connect material properties to recovery performance

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.contribution: examines how public and private actors make and implement sustainability policy, a concrete institutional dimension of lower-impact industrial transition

ENSENVI212.name: Soils & Aquifers
ENSENVI212.contribution: uses field and laboratory analyses to study soil properties, remediation and aquifers as material and environmental systems

ENSENVI213.name: Earth System Science Tools
ENSENVI213.contribution: uses system modelling, proxies and isotope tracers to analyse linked Earth-system processes and greenhouse-gas pathways

ENSENVI311.name: Environmental Biogeochemistry
ENSENVI311.contribution: studies aqueous and mineral biogeochemical processes, water treatment and resource recovery using geochemical modelling

ENSENVI312.name: Earth's Resources
ENSENVI312.contribution: conducts advanced research on resources, geothermal energy, carbon capture and waste storage

ENSGATE101.name: Sustainability Essentials I
ENSGATE101.contribution: establishes physics, chemistry, materials, mathematics and modelling foundations for sustainability problems

ENSGATE201.name: Sustainability Essentials II
ENSGATE201.contribution: extends the sustainability foundation through waves, chemistry and materials science in an applied project

ENSSUST111.name: Climate Change
ENSSUST111.contribution: examines climate drivers, impacts, mitigation, renewable energy and carbon storage as the context for lower-impact production

ENSSUST112.name: Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy
ENSSUST112.contribution: directly evaluates environmental impacts of products and processes across their lifecycle and develops circular-economy planning

ENSSUST211.name: Energy & Sustainability
ENSSUST211.contribution: studies energy conversion technologies and their use in renewable systems before applied system design

ENSSUST311.name: Renewable System Design
ENSSUST311.contribution: assesses energy-use patterns and technically and economically evaluates solar, wind and bioenergy system designs

HCBGATE101.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
HCBGATE101.contribution: introduces biochemistry, macromolecules, cells and DNA as a biological foundation for molecular and biotechnology questions

HCBLIFE211.name: Molecular Cell Biology
HCBLIFE211.contribution: examines cellular structure, metabolism, bioenergetics and molecular regulation to ground the biological applications

HCBLIFE213.name: Biochemistry
HCBLIFE213.contribution: directly studies proteins, sugars, lipids, nucleic acids, metabolic pathways and biotechnology applications

HCBLIFE214.name: Life Science Laboratory
HCBLIFE214.contribution: provides biochemical and molecular laboratory work with proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics

alignment.rationale: Both study biomolecular structure, enzymes and carbohydrates. UCR emphasises metabolism and biochemical function, while Groningen adds engineering applications and an integrated practical.
Both establish calculus and mathematical tools for later scientific work; UCR is general rather than chemistry- and engineering-specific.
Both develop numerical solution methods; UCR provides general computational mathematics rather than chemical-engineering applications.
Both use matrices, vectors and linear systems in quantitative work. Groningen combines linear algebra with multivariable calculus for chemistry.
Both use differential equations, Laplace transforms and feedback to study dynamic responses. Groningen applies them to chemical plants and industrial control equipment.
Both examine societal and institutional choices in sustainability. Groningen centres green chemistry and responsible innovation; UCR uses sustainability governance cases across sectors.
Both use life-cycle assessment to evaluate products and processes. UCR also considers circular-economy strategies. Groningen applies the method to chemical production.
Both address product development and evaluation; UCR teaches general consumer-product design rather than chemical product formulation and industrial production.

academicConstruction: Earth System Science Tools and Consumer Product Design move to term six. Renewable System Design moves to term four after the earlier gateway and Energy & Sustainability. Linear Systems adds applied dynamics. Replacing the unavailable external-partner sustainability project and two less pertinent pathology and general data courses makes room for Linear Systems, Linear Algebra and Energy & Sustainability. The one programme has seven advanced courses; distinctness between alternatives is not applicable. Reconsidered the second candidate across chemistry and materials, geochemical laboratory work, recycling separations and quantitative systems. They cannot sustain reactor engineering, unit operations, thermodynamics and process design. Timing is not the rejection basis.
